body: note: we should also specify that |entry|'s parent is now |new_directory|. Not sure how this should be worded until we have resolution on #59
Hmm, this results in somewhat convoluted overloading I thought we were trying to move away from. @domenic what do you think? Should this use a dictionary?
Also generally we don't follow Python and instead use camelCase for variable names.

I think the overloading might be OK here, although you could reduce it by combining the latter two into `move(FileSystemDirectoryHandle destinationDirectory, optional USVString newEntryName)`.

In terms of API design, I think all of the following are worth considering:

- Positional parameters, varying order (this proposal):
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt")`
  - `fileHandle.move(directoryHandle)`
  - `fileHandle.move(directoryHandle, "renamed.txt")`
- Positional parameters, consistent order (this will choke on https://github.com/plinss/widlparser/issues/79 but is still valid...)
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt")`
  - `fileHandle.move(undefined, directoryHandle)`
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt" directoryHandle)`
- Directory in an options bag (still requires overloading)
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt")`
  - `fileHandle.move({ directory: directoryHandle })`
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt", { directory: directoryHandle })`
- Options bag for everything
  - `fileHandle.move({ name: "renamed.txt"} )`
  - `fileHandle.move({ directory: directoryHandle })`
  - `fileHandle.move({ name: "renamed.txt", directory: directoryHandle })`
- Separate out move within directory vs. move to a new directory
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt")` (or maybe `fileHandle.rename("renamed.txt")`)
  - `fileHandle.moveTo(directoryHandle)`
  - `fileHandle.moveTo(directoryHandle, "renamed.txt")`
- Path-based version?? Seems counter to how much of the rest of the API works, but is more what I would expect from other FS APIs.
  - `fileHandle.move("renamed.txt")`
  - `fileHandle.move(directoryHandle.resolve(fileHandle.name))` (not great...)
  - `fileHandle.move(directoryHandle.resolve("renamed.txt"))`

On balance I think all of these are pretty reasonable, including the current proposal.

Apologies if this has been discussed before; I didn't see it in a quick skim of the several issues and PRs that seem to be about this feature.

On Chromium we already support `move()` for files within the OPFS, so if there's not a strong preference towards any one option I'd prefer to not make any breaking changes. Combining the latter two to make `newEntryName` optional seems reasonable, though, and wouldn't be a breaking change.

If we're convinced we need to change this, the options bag would be my preference since it's more extensible if we want to add more options in the future (e.g. "should this overwrite an existing file at this location?").

Regarding the `rename()` and `moveTo` proposals, I had previously proposed a separate `rename()` method for the first case, (i.e. `fileHandle.rename("renamed.txt")`) but received feedback from developers that a consolidated `move()` method was preferred.

I would especially recommend against a path-based version, since I think it could be confusing to only support relative paths and absolute paths don't make sense outside of the OPFS and won't make sense once sites have access to multiple OPFS instances when Storage Buckets is eventually supported. I'd much rather make it easier to get the destination directory through a convenience method like the one proposed here https://github.com/WICG/file-system-access/issues/378
If there are already developers using and happy with the current proposal, then yeah, I think that tips the balance toward it. It's pretty nice anyway.
And if we add even more options we overload the first argument with a dictionary that accepts everything? (I.e., we end up supporting the status quo and the "options bag".)
It's not the most pretty, but it seems reasonable enough to me
